This Appeal Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

Challenging judgment and award dated 23.02.2019 passed by Addl. Senior Civil Judge & Additional Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Ranebennur, in MVC No.1737/2015, this appeal is filed by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Addl. Senior Civil Judge & Additional Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Ranebennur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts as stated are that in an accident that occurred on 27.07.2015 due to collision between motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-17/EM-7624 and another motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-14/Y-2721, claimant-rider of 1 s t motorcycle sustained grievous injuries.
Despite taking treatment, he did not recover fully and sustained permanent physical disability.
3. Alleging loss of earning capacity, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act against owner and insurer of offending motorcycle.
4. Even on service of notice, owner did not enter appearance.
He was placed exparte.
Respondent-insurer filed objections denying date, time, place and manner of occurrence of accident as well as age, occupation and earning of claimant.

Issuance of insurance policy was admitted and violation of policy condition was alleged.
5. Thereafter, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of claimant as PW1 and Dr.Umanath Ullal as PW2 and two others as PWs.3 and 4.
Exhibits P1 to P36 were marked.
Respondent did not lead oral evidence.
Copy of insurance policy was marked with consent as Exhibit R1.
6. On consideration, Tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of both motorcycles and claimant was entitled for compensation.
But, Tribunal held that claimant had contributed to extent of 80% and insurer was liable to pay compensation only to extent of 20%.

7. It assessed compensation as follows:

Aggrieved by apportionment of negligence as well as seeking for enhancement of compensation, claimant is in appeal.

9. Shri Chandrashekhar M.Hosamani, learned counsel appearing for claimant-appellant submitted that, Tribunal did not award adequate compensation towards pain and suffering, towards attendant and incidental charges, towards loss of income during layoff period and loss of amenities.

It was further submitted even monthly income assessed was on lower side and though disability sustained was assessed by PW2-Doctor at 50% to limb, Tribunal considered meager loss of earning capacity at 8.75% and sought enhancement.
It was submitted that accident occurred on collision between two motorcycles.
As police after investigation filed charge-sheet against both riders, tribunal was not justified in apportioning negligence against claimant to extent of 80%.
Therefore, sought for setting aside of said finding.
10. On other hand, Shri N.R.Kuppelur, learned counsel for respondent-insurer submitted that on over all consideration, award passed by Tribunal was adequate and no enhancement was called for.

It was submitted that since claimant did not lead any specific evidence in support of income,
assessment of same by tribunal was justified.
It was also submitted that rate of interest awarded by Tribunal was excessive and would offset claim for enhancement and sought for dismissal.

11. Insofar as apportionment of negligence it was submitted that, tribunal on consideration of fact that claimant had come on wrong side and dashed against another motorcycle, rightly apportioned negligence and no interference was called for.

12. Heard learned counsel for both parties and perused judgment and award of Tribunal.

13. From above submission, occurrence of accident due to involvement of two motorcycles leading to injuries sustained by claimant and claimant sustaining permanent physical disability are not in dispute.
Issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on date of accident is also not in dispute.
Tribunal apportioned negligence to extent of 80% against claimant.
Claimant is challenging said assessment and also for enhancement.
There is no appeal by insurer.
Only claimant is seeking for enhancement.

Hence, point that arise for consideration are:
"1.
Whether apportionment of negligence by Tribunal calls for interference?

2. Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
14.

From impugned award, it is seen that Tribunal on perusal of Exhibit P5-Accident spot sketch which reveals that rider of motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-17/EM-7624 (i.e., claimant herein) had turned motorcycle at an acute angle to his right side, cross over and dashed against other motorcycle at other end of road apportioned negligence against claimant only to extent of 80%.
Finding is with reference to evidence on record.
Merely on ground that, charge-sheet is filed against both vehicles, tribunal is not bound to hold both vehicles equally responsible.
It is empowered to consider evidence on record and apportion negligence, which in this case it has done rightly.
No interference is called for.
Accordingly, point no.1 is answered in negative.

Point no.2:
15.

Insofar as quantum of compensation, it was stated that claimant aged 38 years working as agriculturist and milk vendor was earning Rs.25,000/- per month and sustained fracture of left humerus bone, left scapula bone, fracture of L1 and L2 vertebra and fracture of left maxilla and zygoma bones.
16. Tribunal has awarded meager sum of Rs.10,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Considering number of fractures, compensation towards pain and suffering is enhanced to Rs.70,000/-.
Tribunal has awarded sum of Rs.90,085/- towards complete reimbursement of - 10 - amount spent towards medical expenses.
No enhancement is called for.
Claimant has taken inpatient treatment for a period of 7 days.
Tribunal has awarded sum of Rs.10,000/- towards attendants and incidental charges which appears just and proper and no enhancement is called for.
Though claimant had stated that he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month, same is not supported by any specific evidence.
In absence of specific evidence, tribunal would be justified in assessing it notionally.
But notional income for year 2015 is Rs.8,000/- as per norms adopted by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for settlement of cases before Lok Adalath.

Therefore, tribunal would Shantanagouda A G S/O A G Benakappa vs Srinivas.G.T S/O Ganeshappa K on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78271421/
4 not be justified in taking it at Rs.5,000/-.

sentences.text: It has to be considered at Rs.8,000/-.
17. Claimant sustained fractures of left humerus bone, left scapula bone, fracture of L1 and L2 vertebra and fracture of left maxilla and - 11 - zygoma bones.

PW2/Dr.Umanath Ullal assessed disability to extent of 20% to left upper limb, 15%
to lumbar spine region and 15% to scull.
PW2- Dr.Umanath Ullal is a orthopedic surgeon.
Assessment of disability due to fracture to scull would not be justified.
However, considering occupation and disability assessed to left upper limb and to lumbar spine region, loss of earning capacity assessed by Tribunal at 8.75% would be grossly inadequate.
It would be appropriate to consider it at 18%.

Thus future loss of income would be as follows:
"Rs.8,000/- x 18% x 12 x 15=Rs.2,59,200/-."
18.
Normally fractures take about 3 months to heal.
Considering said period as layoff, claimant would be entitled to sum of Rs.24,000/- towards loss of income during layoff period.
Tribunal has awarded sum of Rs.10,000/- towards loss of - 12 - amenities.
Considering nature of fractures and extent of disability assessed, award towards same is inadequate.
It is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.

19. Thus, claimant is entitled for re-assessed compensation as follows:-

1. Pain and suffering 70,000/-

2 . Attendant and Incidental 10,000/-
 charges 3.

Medical expenses 90,085/-
4. Loss of income during laid 24,000/-
 up period 5.

Future loss of income 2,59,200/-
6. Loss of amenities 50,000/-

Total: Rs.5,03,285/-

Insofar as rate of interest, this Court in case of Shriram General Insurance Company Limited,
Rajasthan V/s Smt.Laxmi and others reported in (2018) 8 AKR 808, has held rate of interest awardable in a claim petition arising under Motor Vehicles Act has to be at 6%.

Therefore,
- 13 - rate of interest awarded by tribunal is reduced to 6%.

21. In result, I pass following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.
 ii) Judgment and award dated  23.02.2019, passed by Addl. Senior Civil Judge and AMACT, Ranebennur, in MVC no.1737/2015 is modified.
 iii) Claimant is held entitled for  reassessed compensation of Rs.5,03,285/- with interest at rate of 6% p.a. from date of claim petition till date of deposit as against Rs.2,08,835/- awarded by Tribunal.
iv) Directions issued by tribunal regarding apportionment and release of compensation would proportionately apply to enhanced compensation also.
- 14 - iv) Insurer is directed to deposit balance compensation within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
